title: Making a false document
old_text: Section 463 defined forgery; Section 464 detailed making a false document or electronic record dishonestly or fraudulently.
new_text: Consolidates making a false document or electronic record with intent to cause damage or injury, or support any claim or title.
punishment_old: Definition provision (punished under Section 465: up to 2 years, or fine, or both)
punishment_new: Definition and constituent elements provision; sentencing provided under Section 336
explanation: BNS Section 335 consolidates IPC Sections 463 and 464 defining the creation of false documents and false electronic records. It covers unauthorized alteration, digital tampering, and dishonest execution of documents.

title: Forgery
old_text: Whoever commits forgery shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
new_text: Punishment for forgery of documents or electronic records.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both
explanation: BNS Section 336 replaces IPC Section 465 as the primary sentencing section for general forgery. It applies to fraudulent creation or manipulation of non-aggravated documents and records.

title: Forgery of record of Court or of public register, etc.
old_text: Forgery of a document purporting to be a record or proceeding of or in a Court of Justice, or a register of birth, baptism, marriage or burial.
new_text: Forgery of a record of Court of Justice, public register, certified copy, power-of-attorney or official register.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine
explanation: BNS Section 337 corresponds to IPC Section 466 penalizing forgery of official judicial decrees, judicial proceedings, or vital statutory registries. It attracts up to 7 years imprisonment due to the breach of public trust in official records.

title: Forgery of valuable security, will, etc.
old_text: Forgery of a document purporting to be a valuable security, or a will, or an authority to adopt or give receipt.
new_text: Forgery of a document purporting to be a valuable security, will, authority to adopt, or acquittance.
punishment_old: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine
punishment_new: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine
explanation: BNS Section 338 replaces IPC Section 467 protecting testamentary instruments, negotiable instruments, property deeds, and valuable securities against forgery. It carries severe penalties extending up to life imprisonment.

title: Forgery for purpose of cheating
old_text: Committing forgery, intending that the document or electronic record forged shall be used for the purpose of cheating.
new_text: Forgery of document or electronic record with intent that it shall be used for cheating.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine
explanation: BNS Section 339 replaces IPC Section 468 for fabricating forged documents specifically intended to defraud or cheat victims. It is routinely paired with cheating charges in financial and white-collar fraud prosecutions.

title: Forgery for purpose of harming reputation
old_text: Committing forgery, intending that the document or electronic record forged shall harm the reputation of any party.
new_text: Committing forgery intending or knowing it is likely to harm the reputation of any party or character.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years, and fine
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 3 years, and fine
explanation: BNS Section 340 replaces IPC Section 469 penalizing defamatory forgeries, deepfakes, or altered documents fabricated to malign personal reputation or professional integrity.

title: Forged document or electronic record and using it as genuine
old_text: Section 470 defined forged document; Section 471 punished fraudulently or dishonestly using it as genuine.
new_text: Consolidates definition of forged document or electronic record and punishment for fraudulently using as genuine.
punishment_old: Punished in the same manner as if forged the document
punishment_new: Punished in the same manner as if the offender had forged such document or electronic record
explanation: BNS Section 341 merges IPC Sections 470 and 471. A person who utters, tenders, or presents a forged document knowing it to be counterfeit is penalized identically to the original counterfeiter.

title: Making or possessing counterfeit seal, etc., with intent to commit forgery
old_text: Section 472 (counterfeit seal for valuable securities: life/7 yrs); Section 473 (counterfeit seal for general forgery: up to 7 yrs).
new_text: Consolidates making, counterfeiting, or possessing seals, plates, or dies with intent to commit forgery.
punishment_old: General: up to 7 years; valuable security: imprisonment for life or up to 7 years, and fine
punishment_new: General: up to 7 years and fine; valuable security: imprisonment for life or up to 7 years, and fine
explanation: BNS Section 342 merges IPC Sections 472 and 473. Fabricating or possessing counterfeit rubber stamps, government seals, embossed dies, or digital cryptographic signing keys intended for forgery carries up to life imprisonment.

title: Having possession of document described in section 337 or 338, knowing it to be forged and intending to use it as genuine
old_text: Having possession of a forged record of Court or public register (466) or valuable security/will (467) with intent to use as genuine.
new_text: Possession of forged court record, public register, valuable security or will, knowing it to be forged and intending to use it as genuine.
punishment_old: Court record: up to 7 years and fine; valuable security: imprisonment for life or up to 7 years, and fine
punishment_new: Court record: up to 7 years and fine; valuable security: imprisonment for life or up to 7 years, and fine
explanation: BNS Section 343 replaces IPC Section 474 penalizing possession of forged court proceedings, registries, wills, or valuable securities. Clandestinely holding forged deeds with intent to utter them attracts severe penal liability.

title: Counterfeiting device or mark used for authenticating documents, or possessing counterfeit marked material
old_text: Section 475 (marks for valuable securities: life/7 yrs); Section 476 (marks for other documents: up to 7 yrs).
new_text: Consolidates counterfeiting devices, watermarks, authentication holograms, or marks on documents, and possessing such marked materials.
punishment_old: Valuable security: imprisonment for life or up to 7 years; other: up to 7 years and fine
punishment_new: Valuable security: imprisonment for life or up to 7 years; other documents: up to 7 years and fine
explanation: BNS Section 344 merges IPC Sections 475 and 476. It penalizes faking watermarks, security threads, holograms, or authentication seals on official parchment, paper, or electronic media.

title: Fraudulent cancellation, destruction, etc., of will, authority to adopt, or valuable security
old_text: Fraudulently or dishonestly cancelling, destroying, defacing or secreting any will, authority to adopt, or valuable security.
new_text: Dishonestly cancelling, destroying, defacing or secreting any will, adoption authority, or valuable security.
punishment_old: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine
punishment_new: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine
explanation: BNS Section 345 replaces IPC Section 477 punishing the deliberate destruction, shredding, burning, or concealment of wills or title deeds to defeat rightful heirs or creditors.

title: Falsification of accounts
old_text: Clerk, officer or servant wilfully and with intent to defraud destroying, altering, mutilating or falsifying any book, paper, writing or account.
new_text: Falsification of accounts, ledgers, digital registers or financial records by any clerk, employee, officer or servant with intent to defraud.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 7 years, or fine, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 7 years, or fine, or both
explanation: BNS Section 346 replaces IPC Section 477A for corporate and accounting fraud. Cooking books, ledger doctoring, fabricating false expense vouchers, or manipulating ERP database entries by employees is punishable with up to 7 years imprisonment.

title: Property mark and using a false property mark
old_text: Section 479 (property mark definition), 480 & 481 (using false property mark), 482 (punishment: up to 1 year or fine).
new_text: Consolidates property mark definitions and punishment for marking movable property or packages falsely to deceive buyers.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both
explanation: BNS Section 347 merges IPC Sections 479 through 482. It protects commercial branding and product marks by penalizing anyone who uses false property marks to deceive consumers regarding ownership or origin.

title: Tampering with property mark with intent to cause injury
old_text: Section 483 (counterfeiting mark used by another: 2 yrs), 484 (mark used by public servant: 3 yrs), 485 (making/possessing die for property mark: 3 yrs).
new_text: Consolidates counterfeiting property marks, defacing public servant verification marks, and possessing tools or dies for marking property.
punishment_old: Private mark: up to 2 years; public servant mark: up to 3 years and fine; possessing die: up to 3 years and fine
punishment_new: Private mark: up to 2 years and fine; public mark / die apparatus: up to 3 years and fine
explanation: BNS Section 348 merges IPC Sections 483, 484, and 485. It penalizes faking property marks used by competitors, defacing marks affixed by public inspectors (such as BIS or customs stamps), and fabricating marking dies.

title: Counterfeiting a property mark used by another, or selling goods with counterfeit property mark
old_text: Section 486 (selling goods with counterfeit mark: 1 yr), 487 (making false mark upon package: 3 yrs), 488 (punishment for making use of false mark: 3 yrs).
new_text: Consolidates selling, exposing, or possessing goods bearing counterfeit property marks or making deceptive marks on packaging.
punishment_old: Selling: up to 1 year (repeat: 3 years); false mark on package: up to 3 years and fine
punishment_new: Selling counterfeit goods: up to 1 year or fine; fraudulent packaging mark: up to 3 years, or fine, or both
explanation: BNS Section 349 merges IPC Sections 486, 487, and 488 into an exhaustive commercial anti-counterfeiting provision. Trafficking in counterfeit branded merchandise or deceptively packaging goods to mislead consumers is strictly penalized.

title: Making a false mark upon any receptacle containing goods
old_text: Tampering with or making a false mark upon any package, receptacle or casing containing goods to deceive customs or purchasers.
new_text: Tampering with or making a false mark upon any receptacle, crate or container to cause belief that it contains goods which it does not contain.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both
explanation: BNS Section 350 replaces IPC Section 489 penalizing container fraud. Falsely marking crates, barrels, or cargo containers regarding weight, origin, or contents attracts imprisonment up to 3 years or fine.
